gaps.sentence: ___ of my parents speaks French, so I translate for them.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of' = not one and not the other (two people).

gaps.sentence: It's the first time I've ___ eaten oysters.
gaps.explanation: 'The first time + present perfect + ever' emphasises novelty.

gaps.sentence: The museum charges for entry; ___, under-twenties visit free.
gaps.explanation: 'However' marks the contrast between paying and free.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two passwords works — try the other one.
gaps.hint: not one and not the other
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' = not either of them.

gaps.sentence: He talks as if he ___ the owner of the place.
gaps.explanation: 'As if he were' — subjunctive for an unreal comparison.

gaps.sentence: She made me ___ my homework before dinner.
gaps.explanation: 'make somebody do' — bare infinitive after the object.

gaps.sentence: The project ran ___ of money halfway through.
gaps.explanation: 'Run out of' = use up the supply.

gaps.sentence: She speaks English ___ than her brother.
